subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the angle between the lines joining the origin to the points of intersection of the curve x²+2xy+y²+2x+2y−5=0 and the line 3x−y+1=0.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.24 — LAQ chapter 2 Pair of Straight Lines (the HOMOGENISATION run, book pp.24-26), answer 12, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: TS 18 · AP M,J-16. THE MARK SPLIT IS THE BOOK'S: this answer carries printed margin tags. It is one of only TWO answers in the whole chapter that do — answer 12 on book p.24 (printed 1+1+2+1+2) and answer 15 on book p.26 (printed 1+1+1+1+1+2). Both are HOMOGENISATION answers, and both total 7. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. NOTE: Pair of Straight Lines holds TWO Section-C slots — the book's chapter header reads '7+7=14 Marks' and the IPE Blue Print (book p.3) gives it 14 marks, all in Section C and none in Section A or B, so it is an LAQ-ONLY unit and the only 1B unit besides Matrices-on-1A to carry two long slots. The chapter runs book pp.19-26 and its boundary was walked: p.27 opens LAQ chapter 3, D.C's & D.R's. Paper position: Maths-1B Section C runs Q18-Q24 at 7 marks each, answer any 5 of 7. Re-cut to the 8-mark Section-C form of the 2026-27 pattern (TGBIE model paper w.e.f. 2026-27): the extra mark goes to Apply the cosθ formula.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you do to the line first, and what formula finishes it.

steps.label: Clear the line to = 1
steps.margin_note: First mark. Move everything so the line reads (something)/(constant) = 1. Nothing else in the method works until the line is in that form.
steps.memory_tip: Rearrange the line so it reads (something)/(constant) = 1. Nothing works until it is in that form.

recall.must_convey: That the given line is rearranged into the form (expression)/(constant) = 1.
accept: rearrange the line so it equals one
take the constant across and divide so the right side is one
write the line as something over something equals one
line ni equals one form lo raayali
make the line equal to one first

steps.why: Homogenisation only works on a line written as something = 1, because every term of the curve has to be raised to degree two by multiplying by that 1. Clearing the line to that form is therefore the first move every time.
common_mistakes: Leaving the line as ax + by + c = 0 and multiplying by it directly.
Dividing by the wrong constant and losing a sign.

steps.label: Write the homogenised equation
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Raise every term of the curve to degree two: the linear terms are multiplied by that 1 once, and the constant term by it TWICE. The second-degree terms are left alone.
steps.memory_tip: Raise every term to degree two: linear terms times that 1 ONCE, the constant TWICE.

recall.must_convey: That the linear terms are multiplied by the '= 1' expression once and the constant twice.
accept: multiply the linear terms by the bracket once and the constant by it squared
homogenise so every term becomes second degree
the constant gets the bracket squared
linear terms ki okasari, constant ki square
write the homogenised equation

steps.why: A second-degree equation in x and y with NO constant and NO linear term always represents two lines through the ORIGIN — which is exactly what the question asks about. Homogenising manufactures that equation from the curve and the chord.
common_mistakes: Multiplying the constant by the bracket only once.
Multiplying the second-degree terms as well, which raises them to degree four.

steps.label: Simplify to ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Expand everything and collect. The result must have no constant and no linear term — if either survives, a term was homogenised wrongly.
steps.memory_tip: The result must have NO constant and no linear term — if either survives, a term was raised wrongly.

recall.must_convey: That expanding and collecting gives a pure second-degree equation in x and y.
accept: expand everything and collect into a x squared plus two h x y plus b y squared
simplify until only the second degree terms are left
there must be no constant and no linear term
expand chesi collect cheyyali, constant undakoodadu
this gives the pair of lines through the origin

steps.why: The absence of a constant and a linear term is the CHECK that the homogenisation was done right, and it is also what guarantees both lines pass through the origin.
common_mistakes: A constant term surviving, which means the squaring was missed.
Sign slip when expanding a squared bracket.

steps.label: Apply the cosθ formula
steps.margin_note: The last four marks on the 2026-27 paper — printed in the book as '1 Mark' for writing the cosθ formula and '2 Marks' for carrying it through to the angle; the eighth mark of the new pattern goes here too. Note this formula uses 2h, not h — reading the wrong one is the commonest slip in the whole chapter.
steps.memory_tip: Write the cos θ formula out before substituting; the formula itself carries a mark.
lines: On comparing with ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0, we get a = 25, b = 1, 2h = −14
∴ cosθ = |a + b| / √((a − b)² + (2h)²), where θ is the angle between the required lines

lines.text: ∴ Angle between the lines is θ = Cos⁻¹(13/√193)

recall.must_convey: That cosθ = |a+b|/√((a−b)² + (2h)²) is applied to give θ = Cos⁻¹(13/√193).
accept: use cos theta equals mod a plus b over root a minus b whole squared plus two h whole squared
compare to get a b and two h then apply the cosine formula
the angle is cos inverse thirteen over root one ninety three
cos theta formula apply cheyyali
read off a b and two h and substitute

steps.why: The formula carries 2h rather than h because ax² + 2hxy + by² writes the cross coefficient as 2h — so the number read straight off the equation IS 2h, and must not be halved again.
common_mistakes: Using h instead of 2h in the square root.
Forgetting the modulus and producing a negative cosine.
